verdicts.finding: F-timing has moved, not been resolved. Freezing the held-out example text from the cut's opening keeps to the freeze concept: once approved, an example is changed only by the architect. Freezing the judgment folder with the first check of any kind does not keep to it. Held-out checks become frozen when some other check is seen to fail, whether or not they exist yet or have failed themselves. That breaks 'an example is frozen only once its check has been seen to fail'. Two cases follow. A held-out check bound after the first freeze is refused to its check-writer and left to the architect, who has no part in realizing checks. That covers a check-writer still working in parallel (this cut dispatched three at once) and the cold replacement of a burned held-out case under 0103. Visible checks freeze one at a time as each is named; held-out checks should freeze by the same act, once seen to fail. Failing case: open, freeze one visible check, then the check-writer writes a new file in the judgment folder. It must be allowed until that held-out check is itself frozen.

MEANING QUESTION: under the freeze, who writes a burned held-out case's cold replacement (0103 says the illustrator) and its check (the check-writer)? The held-out text, and in this realization the judgment folder, are frozen to everyone but the architect until integration.

MEANING QUESTION: supersession says a concept 'or a bounded context's description … while a cut realizing it is frozen [changes] only by the architect'. Does that cover the description of a context a frozen cut lies in? OBSERVED: the delivered journal lets the lead supersede that description during the freeze; the freeze concept lists only examples, checks and concepts.

The gate fails open when `workPackage frozen` cannot be read. Inside a repository that has a ledger, any act that breaks the reading (finding (c)) turns the whole freeze off. Failing closed there would remove the escalation.
lsp `rename` and `rename_file` from an unfrozen file rewrite references in other files, frozen checks included (INFERRED from LSP semantics). The gate reads only `file` and `new_name`.
A write to `proc://<id>` sends a program to a running pty shell, and the gate never reads it. Contrived evasion.
Paths built from parts in eval or bash (`'design/examples/library/' + 'renewal.md'`) pass the gate (OBSERVED). Contrived.
ast_edit `paths` entries given as `file://` URLs pass the gate (OBSERVED). Whether omp accepts them is not verified.
Formatters run with --write, and `git stash`/`reset`/`checkout <branch>`, can change frozen files without naming them. These changes are incidental, not attempts.
Journal storage files under design/journal/ are not gated. A non-architect's direct `write` of a supersede event file would bypass the capability's refusal. Contrived.
Concepts named only by held-out examples are not frozen: frozen.ts takes concepts from the visible examples only.

Freezing checks depends on the lead calling `freeze`. OBSERVED in the ledger: no check of this cut was frozen until 2026-10-12T00:45:23Z, after the first judgment, so the build ran with its checks unfrozen. Nothing refuses a builder's dispatch while a cut has no frozen check, and under this realization the judgment folder stays open until then.

The visible F-timing case binds only 'frozen at the first freeze', not 'a held-out check frozen only once it has been seen red', which its title claims. The F-route case binds `paths` arrays and direct shell naming only.
